newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum shipments off 8.4 percent Jan-July.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum shipments off 8.4 percent Jan-July.

text.p: Net industry shipments of aluminum mill products in the United States totaled 8.89 billion lbs (4,032,440 tonnes) in the first seven months of the year, down 8.4 percent from the 1995 total of 9.703 billion pounds, Aluminum Association reported.
Domestic shipments of ingot and mill products, totaling 10.3 billion lbs, decreased 6.2 percent from the prior year.
Domestic shipments of sheet, plate and foil fell 10 percent to 6.183 billion lbs. Extruded shapes and tube shipments dipped 2.5 percent to 1.846 billion lbs.

U.S exports of aluminum ingot and mill products, reported at 1.7 billion lbs through July, increased 0.2 percent from the previous year, while imports declined 14.8 percent to 3.34 billion lbs over the same period.
Estimated industry net new orders, totaling 9.979 billion lbs (4,526,403 tonnes) through eight months of 1996, were less than one percent above the previous year's level of 9.956 billion lbs.
August industry orders of 1.306 billion lbs (592,392 tonnes) were up 2.4 percent from the revised July total of 1.275 billion.
New orders of domestic can stock in August fell just 0.1 percent in August, while orders for other sheet and plate were up 4.6 percent.
Month-end U.S. producer inventory totaled 1.55 billion lbs of ingot and 760 million pounds of scrap in July.
